attempts.prompt:
Use case: compositing. Image1 is the sole authority for clothing, pose, hair, expression, light, and crop; Image2 provides only the mascot identity and anatomy. Transform the human anatomy into a smooth golden-yellow compact near-round mascot head and body, featuring green-ringed black eyes and a mouth matching the source expression. Preserve the real source hair: bareheaded with short brown/grey swept-back hair, receding forehead, and real eyebrows. Retain the actual grey/silver upper-lip moustache and short grey chin goatee/beard, distinguishing fine hair strands from the compact rounded yellow anatomy. The expression must remain serious with a closed mouth, and no spectacles are present. Maintain the dark navy/black open civilian suit, white/pale shirt collar, and dark necktie, preserving the primary note-limited inner garment fastening and coherent front/rear collar overlap with contact shadows. Ensure a clearly rounded short U-shaped lower yellow head that immediately meets the raised/broadened existing neckline, with a very short broad neck transition and minimal throat exposure; avoid any separate yellow neck shaft, pointed V funnel, pinched collar, neck rolls, floating collar, clipping, or cream belly bib. Retain the complete tilted dark frame, opaque photographic backing in its actual primary color, and the attached lower-right cream note with faint indistinct upper marks and actual overlap. All solid surfaces must be opaque, with alpha only outside the complete card silhouette. No invented insignia, text, or accessories are permitted. Fine primary details that are indistinct in the source must remain understated. Keep the exact primary mild angle/roll and grey photographic backing/light and crop. Do not add a cap, shave the chin clean, or introduce military uniform or hidden accessories.
FINAL EXACT SOURCE REQUIREMENT: BAREHEADED short BROWN/GREY swept-back hair with receding forehead and real eyebrow HAIR, actual GREY/SILVER upper-lip MOUSTACHE and short GREY chin GOATEE/BEARD, serious CLOSED mouth, no spectacles. DARK NAVY/BLACK OPEN civilian suit, actual WHITE/PALE shirt collar and DARK necktie, primary note-limited inner garment fastening. Keep exact primary mild angle/roll, grey photographic backing/light and crop. No cap, shaved clean chin, military uniform or hidden accessories. Distinguish real short chin beard hair from compact rounded yellow anatomy; fine hair strands understated.
Retain exact primary head angle, expression, cap shape, real hair and visible clothing/decoration areas. One compact near-round yellow mascot head with a clearly ROUNDED short chin immediately contacting raised broad collar, no V-shaped lower-face funnel or yellow shaft. Preserve actual dark solid cloth and photographic backing opacity. Tiny ambiguous features remain understated; no new badge engraving or decorations hidden behind note. Image1 exact original card; Image2 mascot identity/anatomy only.
Output alpha: genuine transparent RGBA ONLY OUTSIDE the complete original framed portrait silhouette. The photographic BACKING INSIDE the frame is a required OPAQUE surface: preserve its original background color and texture behind the character all the way to the inner frame rim. Never turn the gaps between frame and character into transparent holes or a window. Keep the actual frame angle and rim. Preserve an overlapping paper note, pin or other attachment ONLY when actually visible in this exact source; otherwise do not invent one. Do not invent a new backdrop outside the whole card. Retain source clothing, hair, headgear, lighting and crop at full generated resolution. All originally OPAQUE subject surfaces must remain FULLY OPAQUE (alpha 255): yellow head/body, hair, beard, dark or black clothing, coat lapels, collar, tie, buttons and decorations. Dark cloth is colored material, not transparent background. Never fade garment interiors into semi-transparent patches, holes, white haze or see-through fabric. Keep any genuine source outer-edge alpha falloff only at that actual exterior boundary; preserve actual source transparency rather than making the subject itself translucent.
